exposure: Caesarean section during the second stage of labor
Caesarean section during the active phase of the first stage of labor
outcome: Intraoperative complications (operative time, blood loss, uterine extensions)
Postoperative morbidity (fever, wound infections, hospital stay)
cohort: The study included 90 women who underwent LSCS, divided equally into those undergoing the procedure in the first stage of labor (n=45) and those in the second stage of labor (n=45).
finding: Second-stage caesarean sections are associated with increased intraoperative difficulty, higher maternal morbidity, and poorer neonatal outcomes compared to first-stage caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections performed during the second stage of labor result in significantly longer operative times, greater blood loss, more uterine extensions, increased postoperative fever, wound infections, longer hospital stays, and poorer neonatal outcomes (lower Apgar scores, higher NICU admissions, and more neonatal complications) compared to first-stage caesarean sections.
